title: Trek Domane SL 6 Review — Better Than Roubaix, Defy, Endurace?

takeaways.text: The SL 6 with Shimano 105 Di2 cost £3,900 at publication, with the range starting at £2,800; he noted a Giant Defy with the same groupset and similar carbon wheels was £600 less.
He gives 38 mm tire clearance without mudguards and 35 mm with them; the bike came on 32 mm tires, and he expected a 40 mm tire to be tight.
Semi-internal routing keeps a round alloy bar and stem that are easy to swap; there is in-frame storage with a large lever, plus mudguard, top-tube bento and extra down-tube mounts.
His size 56 with 105 Di2 weighed 8.9 kg on his scales, heavier than he expected; he put its Bontrager carbon wheels at nearly 1,700 g, with a narrow 19.5 mm internal width.
The IsoSpeed decoupler made the saddle very smooth on rough roads, though it is no longer adjustable, so flex depends on rider weight; the front end felt firmer, a bike of two halves.
It lacked urgency: on fast club rides he felt he worked harder to keep up than on a sportier Giant Defy, so he sees it as a bike for maximum comfort and a relaxed fit.

disclosure: The video does not say how the bike was obtained. The description carries affiliate links for a camera, a bike stand, clothing and shoes.
summary: A November 2025 review of a fourth-generation Domane SL 6 with 105 Di2 and Bontrager carbon wheels on the same Gen 4 SL frame as the SL 5 recorded here, with a weigh-in, clearance, storage and ride impressions. The recorded SL 5 uses mechanical Shimano 105, so its weight and wheels can differ.
